metadata.file_name: 1. Lee & Lee. (2025). An Extended Dataset of Educational Quality Across Countries (1970–2023) 3.pdf
metadata.title: An Extended Dataset of Educational Quality Across Countries (1970–2023)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper constructs a cross-country panel dataset (country-year observations) by harmonizing and imputing test-score series and then deriving educational quality indexes for age cohorts. The only explicit weighting described is for the working-age educational quality index (ages 15–64), where population weights are used to aggregate cohort-specific normalized test scores into Q (15–19, 20–24, …, 60–64). The manuscript does not report the use of ILSA-style sampling/survey weights for student-level inference, and the ML imputation step (LASSO) is described as a standard supervised learning procedure with a train/validation split and cross-validation rather than complex-survey estimation. Therefore, analysts should treat the dataset as harmonized/constructed panel data with population-weighted aggregation for Q, not as a survey microdata file requiring student replicate-weight variance estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study is a dataset construction/harmonization paper that imputes missing country-year test-score observations using linear interpolation/extrapolation and a supervised LASSO prediction model, rather than estimating or analyzing ILSA Plausible Values (PV) for student achievement outcomes. Because the dependent variables are constructed harmonized scores (Tscore_INT/Tscore_ML) and derived indexes (Tscore1519_INT/Tscore1519_ML, Q_INT/Q_ML) at the country-year level, PV-specific combining rules are not applicable. Missingness is addressed via interpolation and ML-based prediction, but the paper does not frame this as a PV-multiple-imputation workflow with a standard PV handling category, so PV handling is set to not_applicable and missing-data handling is not_reported in the PV/missing-data schema.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The dataset covers 101 countries and 12 assessment years (1970, 1980, 1984, 1990, 1995, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023), forming 1212 potential country-year observations (101×12). Observed harmonized test-score inputs come from 631 original observed data points across TIMSS (1995–2023; 323), PISA (2000–2022; 245), and earlier IEA/IAEP studies (1970–1991; 63). The analytic panel is balanced via imputation of 581 missing country-year observations (48%) using (i) linear interpolation/extrapolation within each country and (ii) LASSO regression predictions using 501 fully observed World Bank economic/education indicators (from an initial pool of 3442). Countries are excluded if they lack nationally representative samples (explicitly noting China and India) or if key World Bank indicators are missing, which are required for panel construction and imputation.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Best model: LASSO (see outcome_summary for metrics)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Literature synthesis outcome (not student-level prediction), finding that This paper does not estimate educational achievement effects on student-level outcomes; instead, it constructs an extended cross-country educational quality dataset from 1970–2023 by harmonizing mathematics and science test scores from TIMSS and PISA (plus earlier IEA/IAEP studies) onto the TIMSS 1995 metric (mean 500, SD 100). It anchors PISA to the TIMSS scale using equi-percentile linking and then averages mathematics and science to form a single harmonized achievement measure. Missing country-year observations (581 out of 1212; 48%) are filled using two approaches: linear interpolation/extrapolation (Tscore_INT) and a supervised LASSO regression imputation (Tscore_ML) trained on 80% of the data with 20% validation and grid search with tenfold cross-validation to minimize RMSE. The LASSO model reports RMSE of 17.5 and R² of 0.912 (and an out-of-sample RMSE of 15.7 and R² of 0.905), and the two imputation methods show high agreement (correlation 0.967). The working-age educational quality index Q is then computed using population-weighted aggregation across age cohorts with an assumed return parameter derived from wage-return estimates. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is intentionally sparse for ML/predictive findings because the manuscript is primarily a dataset construction and harmonization study (a data paper) rather than an empirical predictive modeling paper with a clearly defined student-level target variable and reported predictive performance for a specified outcome. As a result, there are no distinct target variables for which the schema requires StructuredFinding rows, and confounders/predictors are not extracted as conceptual controls because the LASSO is used for imputing missing harmonized scores rather than for causal or policy-relevant prediction of an educational outcome.
